content: This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Lamivudine is similar to emtricitabine and should not be taken concurrently with this medication. Always check the labels of your HIV medications to ensure they do not contain the same active ingredients as this product. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load measurements, T-cell counts, and hepatitis B virus testing, should be conducted prior to initiating this medication and periodically during its use. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container. Capsules should be kept at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and not stored in the bathroom. The oral solution should be refrigerated and not frozen. If necessary, the solution may be stored at room temperature but must be discarded after three months. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Emtricitabine is used in combination with other HIV medications to control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. However, emtricitabine is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Before starting emtricitabine, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. If using the liquid form, measure the dose carefully with a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is based on your medical condition, the form of the medication (capsule or liquid), and your response to treatment. For children, the dosage may also be based on weight. To achieve the best effect, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, take more or less than prescribed, or stop taking it without your doctor’s approval. Common side effects may include headache, diarrhea, difficulty sleeping, or darkening of the skin on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Rarely, this medication can cause severe, potentially fatal liver and blood problems, such as lactic acidosis. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking emtricitabine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Lamivudine is similar to emtricitabine and should not be taken with this medication. Check the labels on all your HIV medications to ensure they do not contain the same ingredients as this product.
